Because I am 65 and my household is small, I will keep the plan simple and steady rather than do anything complicated. I have many years of experience, and with well irrigation I will rely on stable water and moderate fertilizer instead of pushing for the highest possible input level. For wheat, I will use improved seed, rotary tillage, enough nitrogen to support tillering and grain filling, with phosphorus and potassium at moderate levels, and I will irrigate at key stages because wheat responds clearly to timely water. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I want stronger yield and uniform growth after wheat harvest, and I will keep fertilizer balanced but put a little more nitrogen than wheat. I will also keep pesticide use limited to what is necessary, because I want to control cost and labor while protecting yield. My goal this year is stable production, manageable work, and no unnecessary risk.
